label: agent loop • edit a .docx paragraph whose stored text has Word smart quotes and an em dash
query: In memo.docx, in the paragraph about the payment provider, replace the quoted term "go-live" (including its quotes) with the plain word launch, so the sentence reads: The migration to the new payment provider is on track - the launch remains scheduled for April 14. Don't change anything else in the memo.
notes: The stored paragraph uses “ ” curly quotes and an em dash, and Word split it across two runs. A model that types straight quotes and a hyphen must still succeed in one or two calls: DOCXEditor's normalized-punctuation cascade matches the paragraph, and the result says so. Assertions: 'launch remains scheduled for April 14' landed (with or without the article), the curly-quoted term is gone, and the untouched heading is intact.

commands.command: python3 -c "import zipfile,re; x=zipfile.ZipFile('memo.docx').read('word/document.xml').decode(); t=''.join(re.findall(r'<w:t[^>]*>([^<]*)</w:t>', x)); assert 'launch remains scheduled for April 14' in t, t; assert '\u201cgo-live\u201d' not in t and 'go-live' not in t, t; assert 'Vendor Update Memo' in t and 'Status: Draft' in t, t"
